articles.summary: The MoU signed by leaders of Northern Ireland, Wales, and Scotland signals growing demands for independence and closer EU ties, pressuring Westminster to address their aspirations. Their goals and approaches differ.

articles.headline: India cautions citizens against joining Russian Army
articles.summary: The Indian government strongly discouraged citizens from traveling to Russia to join its army, warning of 'mortal dangers' and misleading job offers from unverified agents.

articles.headline: Mallikarjun Kharge calls for unity; Rahul Gandhi criticizes CEC immunity
articles.summary: At the INDIA bloc meeting, Mallikarjun Kharge stressed unity, while Rahul Gandhi criticized the CEC's 'lifelong blanket immunity'. The bloc aims to defend the Constitution and mobilize people against alleged 'vote theft'.

articles.headline: EC extends SIR dates for Andhra Pradesh and Meghalaya
articles.summary: The Election Commission extended the final electoral roll publication dates for Andhra Pradesh and Meghalaya due to the ongoing special intensive revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.

articles.headline: Bengal SIR tribunal judge wants to quit over long commute
articles.summary: A judge presiding over a West Bengal Special Intensive Revision (SIR) tribunal offered to resign, citing a 70-80 km daily commute. Justice Indrajit Chatterjee is concerned about the deletions of eligible voters.

articles.headline: SC rules out total ban on fireworks for Deepavali
articles.summary: The Supreme Court declined a total ban on fireworks for Deepavali, accepting suggestions for 'green crackers' with lower noise and emissions. The court will consider specific time windows for bursting.

articles.headline: NCERT textbook revives debatable theory on Sengol transfer of power
articles.summary: NCERT's new Class 9 textbook mentions a Sengol handed to Nehru in 1947 as a symbol of power transfer, a theory disputed by historians. The textbook also links national mottos to ancient texts.

articles.headline: Gill stars in India's record 406-run chase vs West Indies
articles.summary: Shubman Gill's unbeaten 223 and Rohit Sharma's century powered India to a historic 406-run chase, the second-highest in ODIs, to beat West Indies by eight wickets and clinch the series.

articles.headline: Indian students among five teams selected for CERN competition
articles.summary: Five Indian school students were selected for CERN's 'Beamline for Schools' competition. Their project focuses on measuring pion charge exchange, a process relevant for neutrino physics.

articles.headline: SpaceX Starship engine failure could impact NASA's moon mission
articles.summary: An engine failure during SpaceX's Starship test flight may affect NASA's timeline for lunar missions. The glitch is critical for the spacecraft's role in the Artemis programme.

articles.headline: Pilot stabs Indian captain in cockpit; Israeli PM hails heroics
articles.summary: A flydubai co-pilot allegedly stabbed captain Smit Machchhar on a Dubai-Tel Aviv flight, causing a 14,300-foot plunge. The jet diverted to Tabuk after a hijack alert. Israeli PM credited Machchhar with fighting back, opening the door, and saving 174 lives.

articles.headline: Monsoon rain over India 4th lowest since 2001, large parts dry
articles.summary: India's southwest monsoon ended with 12.6% below-normal rainfall, recording 759.4mm from June-September. This is the fourth-lowest monsoon since 2001, leaving large parts of the country dry after a weak start and uneven distribution.

articles.headline: Chandra family company pursues tech park to serve TVS Motor
articles.summary: A company owned by Tata Sons chairman N Chandrasekaran's family is developing a ₹330-crore industrial park in Karnataka for TVS Motor Co. This is the second such project, raising corporate governance questions due to non-disclosure to Tata Sons and Tata Trusts boards.

articles.headline: INDIA bloc revives paper ballot demand, lists steps to target CEC
articles.summary: Opposition parties revived their demand to replace EVMs with paper ballots and announced a six-point program to target CEC Gyanesh Kumar and PM Modi. They accuse the government of manipulating voter rolls during special intensive revision (SIR) to subvert electoral integrity.

articles.headline: Cabinet hikes MSP for Rabi crops for 2027-28; oilseeds, pulses gain most
articles.summary: The Centre raised minimum support prices (MSPs) for all six Rabi crops for the 2027–28 marketing season. Safflower, rapeseed, and mustard received the largest price boosts, aiming to ensure remunerative returns to farmers and encourage crop diversification.

articles.headline: MCD seeks govt help to plug gaps in its largest parks
articles.summary: More than 1,000 large parks under the Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD) have only 42 guards and not a single CCTV camera. Following a recent gang rape, MCD is seeking government help to install cameras and deploy more guards to enhance safety.

articles.headline: SP RS poll pick's Gujarat links creates a buzz
articles.summary: The Samajwadi Party on Wednesday named Ram Gopal Yadav and Dhanraj Parimal Nathwani as its Rajya Sabha poll candidates. Nathwani's corporate profile and links to Gujarat political circles created buzz, fueling speculation about SP's strategy.

articles.headline: Spat over child at workplace may have triggered Kathua fratricide
articles.summary: The argument leading to a CISF head constable shooting four colleagues in Kathua, J&K, apparently concerned the presence of his child at their hydropower project workplace. Multiple versions indicate this as the trigger, prompting police and internal CISF investigations.

articles.headline: ED arrests Vatika Group promoters in money laundering probe
articles.summary: The Enforcement Directorate arrested Vatika Group chairman Anil Bhalla and promoter Gautam Bhalla in a money laundering probe linked to alleged fraud with homebuyers. The investigation stems from a Delhi Police FIR alleging fraudulent inducement and non-delivery of plots.

articles.headline: Ex-IAS officer found murdered at home in Bhopal; caretaker missing
articles.summary: A 70-year-old retired IAS officer, Rakesh Agarwal, was found dead with his throat slit at his Bhopal residence. Police suspect his newly hired caretaker, Varun Kumar, who is missing since the incident.

articles.headline: Limp monsoon left swathes of India bone dry, 17th lowest since 1901
articles.summary: India's four-month southwest monsoon ended as the 17th lowest since 1901, with 39% of the country experiencing drought-like conditions. Long dry spells were common in western and peninsular India, raising concerns for agriculture and inflation.

articles.headline: 'Dangerous path': Govt warns Indians against joining Russian forces
articles.summary: India warned its nationals against joining Russian armed forces, including non-public entities, calling it a "dangerous path" and strongly discouraged it. This follows the deaths of 51 Indians in Ukraine and ongoing efforts to secure the discharge of others.

articles.headline: From OG to Gen Z, India’s women quarter-milers Asia’s track queens
articles.summary: India's women's 4x400m relay team won gold at the Asian Games, marking a resurgence for the country's quarter-milers. Veterans like PT Usha and Shiny Abraham Wilson expressed pride as the new generation delivered, breaking old records.

articles.headline: 12-year-old boy riding pillion on bike killed in B’luru accident
articles.summary: A 12-year-old boy, Dikshith, died in Bengaluru after the two-wheeler he was riding pillion on with his grandfather allegedly lost balance and fell on the road when a car suddenly came in their path.

articles.headline: Chennai-based bizman held in fake meds case, inquiry widened
articles.summary: Balasubramanian, a Chennai-based pharmaceutical distributor and business associate of alleged counterfeit drug racket kingpin Prashanth Rajanbabu, was arrested by the Karnataka SIT, becoming the seventh person taken into custody in the case.

articles.headline: KPSC scam: Candidates gave blank cheques for favourable selection, says ED
articles.summary: The ED revealed candidates in the KPSC veterinary officers' recruitment examination scam allegedly paid ₹30-80 lakh for favourable selection, securing unpaid balances with blank cheques. The agency is investigating money laundering by key accused.

articles.headline: Bengaluru's 5-commissionerate plan to be placed before Cabinet
articles.summary: The Karnataka government is expected to place its plan to split the Bengaluru City Police Commissionerate into five units before the Cabinet, creating 6,633 new police posts at a projected cost of ₹764.87 crore.

articles.headline: K’taka rolls out ‘Govt First’ for startups, says Minister Priyank Kharge
articles.summary: Karnataka launched the ‘Government First’ initiative to provide startups opportunities to develop solutions for government departments, improving services and offering early market access. The ₹25 crore initiative aims to support up to 100 startups.

articles.headline: Karnataka govt mulls points-based driving licence system
articles.summary: Karnataka is considering introducing a points-based driving licence system where repeated traffic violations attract penalty points, potentially leading to licence suspension. The system would integrate with e-Challan and include higher fines and mandatory training for offenders.

articles.headline: CCB charges Veeramani with abetment of victim’s suicide
articles.summary: The central crime branch (CCB) of Tamil Nadu police registered a new abetment to suicide case against industrialist R Veeramani, 84, related to the death of a minor in 2004. The case resurfaced after an SMS from a co-accused.

articles.headline: 2 people held for aiding Telangana arms heist; probe on
articles.summary: Telangana police detained two more people, Vinod and Seshu, for allegedly aiding army havildar Upputholla Mallesh in the August 31 theft of arms and ammunition from the Madras Regiment armoury in Secunderabad. Mallesh was arrested earlier.

articles.headline: Madras HC junks police plea to transfer Veeramani probe to CBI
articles.summary: The Madras High Court refused to transfer the POCSO case involving granite baron R Veeramani to the CBI, stating that the SIT constituted by the Tamil Nadu government should be given time to collect evidence.

articles.headline: IPS officer recuses herself from SIT probing Veeramani case
articles.summary: V V Geethanjali, one of four IPS officers on the Special Investigation Team (SIT) probing the Veeramani case, recused herself citing personal reasons. She was part of an earlier investigation into Veeramani under a different police commissioner.

articles.headline: BJP reiterates demand for CBI probe in Veeramani case
articles.summary: The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) reiterated its demand for a CBI probe into the Veeramani case, expressing apprehension that the state SIT would not conduct an independent and effective investigation due to alleged involvement of high-ranking officials.

articles.headline: Former AIADMK Min Semmalai joins TVK with his supporters
articles.summary: Former minister and seasoned AIADMK leader S Semmalai officially joined the ruling Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) with his supporters at a rally in Dharapuram. He cited the rift in AIADMK and denied election opportunities as reasons.

articles.headline: Foreign spouses of Indians not entitled to visa: Kerala HC
articles.summary: The Kerala High Court ruled that a foreign national, even if married to an Indian citizen, has no vested right to demand an Indian visa. The court dismissed a writ plea by a Kerala man and his Pakistani wife seeking a tourist visa.

articles.headline: Mother held for drowning two children in Keralam: Police
articles.summary: Police arrested Nivedya in Kerala for allegedly drowning her two young children, aged five and three. She confessed, claiming the children were a "hindrance" to her quest for a free, independent life and a modeling career.

articles.headline: Andhra to develop Tirupati as global wedding destination
articles.summary: The Andhra Pradesh government plans to develop Tirupati as a global wedding destination, complementing its existing religious tourism ecosystem. The objective is to create an integrated economic activity with facilities for all economic segments.

articles.headline: CCMB study links viral illnesses to Parkinson’s disease
articles.summary: A study by CSIR-Centre for Cellular and Molecular Biology (CCMB) found that infections caused by certain viruses, such as influenza and SARS-CoV-2, are likely to cause neurodegenerative diseases like Parkinson’s. Viruses can promote abnormal protein clumps.

articles.headline: Opposition may put hold on motion to remove CEC Gyanesh Kumar
articles.summary: The Opposition might put on hold its plan to move a motion for the removal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. INDIA bloc leaders prefer political programmes and public outreach over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of the electoral roll.

articles.headline: Ex-min Majithia summoned in ₹6k-cr drug case by Punjab SIT
articles.summary: A Punjab Police Special Investigation Team (SIT), probing a ₹6,000 crore drug case, has summoned senior Akali leader and former minister Bikram Singh Majithia to appear before it on October 5, along with dismissed police officer Jagdish Bhola.

articles.headline: 'How does your system override law?': HC to ECI on Goa deletions
articles.summary: The Bombay High Court questioned the Election Commission of India (ECI) on how "software glitches" justified deleting seven family members from electoral rolls without a hearing, despite their valid Form 8 submissions during the special intensive revision.

articles.headline: INDIA bloc breaking, leaders reject Rahul Gandhi's leadership: Chouhan
articles.summary: BJP leader Shivraj Singh Chouhan claimed the INDIA bloc is crumbling and its leaders have rejected Rahul Gandhi’s leadership. He alleged that the bloc's planned agitations are meant to save "dynasty" rather than democracy.

articles.headline: IISc B’luru slips out of top 250 institutes in global rankings
articles.summary: The Indian Institute of Science (IISc), Bengaluru, has slipped out of the top 250 in the Times Higher Education (THE) World University Rankings 2027, despite improving its scores. It is now placed at 254th, down from 201-250.

articles.headline: 'Too much heat' generated: SC on deletion of CAPF plea
articles.summary: The Supreme Court remarked "Sometimes too much heat is generated out of nothing" as it sought to defuse a controversy over the abrupt deletion of contempt petitions concerning deputation of IPS officers to CAPFs from a cause list.

articles.headline: U.P. tutor booked over video of pupils’ remarks against PM Modi
articles.summary: A private coaching teacher in Uttar Pradesh's Etah district was booked for allegedly filming students making objectionable comments and unsubstantiated allegations against Prime Minister Narendra Modi in a widely circulated video.

articles.headline: Ojhats gets 1-year extension as PIB principal DG
articles.summary: Senior Indian Information Service (IIS) officer Dhirendra Ojha was re-employed as principal director general of the Press Information Bureau (PIB) on a contract basis for one year, until September next year, by the Appointments Committee of the Cabinet.

articles.headline: Luthra brothers offer ₹15L each to families of Goa fire victims
articles.summary: The Luthra brothers, co-owners of Birch by Romeo Lane, a Goa nightclub where a fire claimed 25 lives last December, have offered to compensate each victim's family with ₹15 lakh. The high court is hearing a suo motu writ petition.

articles.headline: Court to hear afresh land-for-jobs case against Lalu, family
articles.summary: A Delhi court will hear afresh from October 14 arguments on framing of charges against former Bihar chief minister Lalu Prasad Yadav, his wife Rabri Devi, and other family members in the alleged land-for-jobs money laundering case.

articles.headline: Gujarat HC denies temporary bail to Asaram to meet wife
articles.summary: The Gujarat High Court on Wednesday rejected a 20-day temporary bail application by convicted rapist and self-styled godman Asaram, who sought release from Jodhpur jail to meet his wife undergoing treatment.

articles.headline: 'Vehicles running on 100% ethanol may hit roads in 2 mths'
articles.summary: Union minister Nitin Gadkari announced that leading automakers are expected to launch flex-fuel vehicles capable of running on 100% ethanol within the next one to two months, as part of India's green mobility transition.

articles.headline: SC: Accused can use unrelied prosecution documents in trial
articles.summary: The Supreme Court held that an accused can not only inspect documents seized but not relied upon by the prosecution, but also have specific documents brought before witnesses during trial if relevant to the defence, settling a contentious procedural issue.

articles.headline: 'It is better that we disband U.P. Police': SC livid over shoddy job
articles.summary: The Supreme Court strongly criticized the Uttar Pradesh police for shoddy investigation, including not recording the name of an accused caught on the spot in an FIR. The court warned it might direct the CBI to take over all criminal cases in the state.

articles.headline: Himanta says sorry as convoy halts ambulance; 4 cops suspended
articles.summary: Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma apologized and suspended four police personnel after his convoy allegedly halted an ambulance in Silchar. He called the incident unacceptable, emphasizing no CM's passage should ever take precedence over urgent care.

articles.headline: NIA begins probe into AQIS bid to recruit from sub-continent
articles.summary: The National Investigation Agency (NIA) launched a probe into an alleged conspiracy by al-Qaeda in the Indian Subcontinent (AQIS) to radicalize and recruit youngsters in the name of 'Ghazwa-e-Hind,' establishing a base in West Bengal.

articles.headline: Multi-state ED raids in ₹200-cr CSR scam
articles.summary: The Enforcement Directorate conducted multi-state raids in Maharashtra, West Bengal, Gujarat, and Delhi-NCR in connection with an alleged ₹200 crore bogus Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) donation racket. Market operators, trustees, and middlemen were targeted.

articles.headline: Plea seeks recall of SC order on challenge to CEC appointment law
articles.summary: An application filed in the Supreme Court sought the recall of an order referring a challenge to the law governing the appointment of the Chief Election Commissioner and Election Commissioners to a Constitution bench. It alleges a likelihood of bias by one of the judges.

articles.headline: A pilot brawl, then rapid descent: Passengers recount chaos on flight
articles.summary: Passengers on flydubai flight FZ1073 recounted chaos after a co-pilot allegedly stabbed the captain. The plane plunged over 30,000 feet before passengers and a reserve crew subdued the attacker and stabilized the aircraft, landing safely in Saudi Arabia.

articles.headline: SC permits green cracker use, keeps barium content issue pending
articles.summary: The Supreme Court permitted the use of "green" firecracker chains (laris) nationwide and specified green crackers, citing public sentiment. However, the more contentious issue of barium-containing green crackers was kept pending for further scientific evaluation.

articles.headline: The UN can still work towards restoring trust
articles.summary: The UN General Assembly's 81st session focuses on "Restoring trust, Managing Transformation." While efficiency reforms are underway, structural reforms, particularly of the UN Security Council (UNSC), are essential to address the trust deficit and ensure representation.

articles.headline: India must urgently get its own AI Safety Institute
articles.summary: India urgently needs its own AI Safety Institute to independently test AI models for risks, develop India-specific benchmarks, and avoid becoming a "rule-taker" in global AI governance. This is crucial for national security, armed forces, and market relevance.

articles.headline: India’s elderly women need better social security cover
articles.summary: India faces a feminization of ageing, with elderly women outnumbering men, often lacking social protection and economic independence. The author advocates for a universal, inflation-indexed social pension and comprehensive care programs for older women.

articles.headline: Forever reneging on ending forever wars
articles.summary: The US withdrawal from Iraq, after more than two decades, continues a familiar pattern of ending "forever wars," echoing its Afghanistan exit. The author questions the impact on West Asian stability, especially amid the ongoing US-Iran conflict.

articles.headline: Pak vows to defend Saudi against Iran-backed Houthis
articles.summary: Pakistan's defence minister stated the country would use "whatever means are available" to defend Saudi Arabia against Iran-backed Houthi rebels, signaling potential direct involvement in the widening regional conflict. This follows intensified Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia.

articles.headline: G20 ministers open talks under strain of Trump tariffs
articles.summary: G20 trade ministers began talks in the United States under strain from President Donald Trump's latest global tariffs, which are casting a pall over the gathering and pushing countries to seek cooperation outside the world's biggest economy.

articles.headline: US top court okays third-country deportations
articles.summary: The US Supreme Court lifted restrictions on the deportations of immigrants to countries that are not their own, while agreeing to hear the issue on its merits in December, potentially affecting immigration policy.

articles.headline: 2 Indians indicted for counterfeit Ozempic smuggling in US
articles.summary: Swapnadip Roy and Vicky Ramancha, Indian nationals, have been indicted by a US federal grand jury for allegedly smuggling and selling counterfeit Ozempic, the popular weight-loss drug, in the United States.

articles.headline: Iran receives US response to its latest offer on ending war
articles.summary: Iranian officials indicated they have received an official US response to Tehran's latest proposal to end the seven-month war, which US President Donald Trump had publicly rejected just days earlier. Iran's President emphasized a 'win-win strategy'.

articles.headline: UK hints Iran role in US air base incident after arrests
articles.summary: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham said there are "strong indications" that Iran played a part in an incident near a US-run air base in England on Sunday, where five men were arrested.

articles.headline: US trade court probes 'forced labour' tariffs by Trump administration
articles.summary: The US Court of International Trade scrutinized the legal and factual underpinnings of President Donald Trump's latest global tariffs. These tariffs were imposed over allegations trading partners aren't doing enough to stop forced labor, facing lawsuits alleging misuse of authority.

articles.headline: Indian among 5 killed in hijacked ship rescue operation
articles.summary: An Indian national and four others who were part of a hijacked tanker's crew were killed in a shootout between pirates and Somali security forces trying to retake the vessel. The deceased was identified as Mohammed Tanweeruz Zaman.

articles.headline: Centre moves to reduce customs collection costs, seeks efficiency
articles.summary: The government is working to reduce the elevated cost of collecting customs duties, which has risen to ₹1.23 for every ₹100 of revenue. This move follows a directive from the Parliamentary Standing Committee on Finance.

articles.headline: China’s divers extend 52-year unbeaten record at Asian Games
articles.summary: China’s divers extended their remarkable Asian Games win unbeaten record stretching back to 1974. Chen Yiwen and Lian Junjie each won gold in the final two diving events to give China a 14th consecutive clean sweep in the sport.

articles.headline: Japan wins penalty shootout in semis, reaches men's football final
articles.summary: Hosts Japan will play reigning champions South Korea for Asian Games men’s football gold after winning a nail-biting semi-final 9-8 on penalties against Uzbekistan. Japan forced extra time with a late goal to make it 1-1.

articles.headline: Saptak, Pranavi make fine start in Asian Games golf
articles.summary: Saptak Talwar shot a 4-under 66 in the first round of the Asian Games men’s golf to be tied third. In women's golf, Pranavi Urs also made a fine start, shooting an excellent 4-under 66 to be second, three shots off China’s leader.

articles.headline: Solitary gold and sporadic bright streaks in Asian Games athletics
articles.summary: India secured only one gold medal in athletics at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games, its fewest since the 2006 Games, along with 9 silver and 14 bronze. This was a disappointing campaign compared to previous editions, despite some personal bests.

articles.headline: Injured Raphinha out of India football match for Brazil
articles.summary: Brazil's Raphinha was released from the national team on Wednesday due to a minor muscle edema on the back of his right thigh. As a precaution, the forward will miss Brazil's upcoming match against India on Saturday.

articles.headline: Ronaldo unhappy with coach, likely to miss Portugal training
articles.summary: Reports suggest Cristiano Ronaldo is unhappy with coach Jorge Jesus, as he missed team training and was only doing gym work. There is doubt about the superstar playing for Portugal.

articles.headline: Lovlina in Asiad final as Indian boxers continue to shine
articles.summary: Lovlina Borgohain secured a spot in the Asian Games boxing middleweight (75kg) final with a gritty comeback win. India has now confirmed six boxing medals, with three gold-medal bouts to come, improving on previous Asiad hauls.

articles.headline: TT’s ad hoc panel halts national ranking points for tournaments
articles.summary: The ad hoc panel overseeing table tennis in India has stripped all national ranking tournaments of their official ranking points ahead of the Panchkula edition, beginning October 6. This follows the sports ministry's derecognition of TTFI.

articles.headline: Djokovic grinds out opening-round win at China Open
articles.summary: Novak Djokovic held his nerve during a tense tie-break to beat Arthur Fils 6-3, 7-6 (7/2) in his opening-round match at the China Open. The 39-year-old Serbian was struggling physically but pushed through the second-set decider.

articles.headline: Shadab Khan likely to lead Pak in T20Is as changes loom
articles.summary: Shadab Khan has emerged as the front-runner to take over Pakistan’s T20 captaincy from Salman Ali Agha, who faces axe from the squad for the shortest format. Information from Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) insiders indicates big changes.

articles.headline: I had thoughts of quitting chess, it was that hard: Olympiad star Savitha
articles.summary: 19-year-old Savitha Shri, after an unbeaten 9/10 score and individual gold at the Fide Chess Olympiad, revealed she considered quitting chess due to past struggles. Her performance helped India win bronze and revived her career.

articles.headline: IndiaAI Mission may be rewired on GPU crunch and rising costs
articles.summary: The government plans to recalibrate the IndiaAI Mission due to delays and escalating costs of critical compute components, particularly GPUs. GPU prices have doubled since March 2024. The IT ministry is now considering buying 3,000 GPUs directly and contracting compute capacity.

articles.headline: Buoyant Q2 consumer demand lifts festive sales outlook
articles.summary: Consumer demand accelerated in the July-September quarter, with strong growth in ACs, refrigerators, washing machines, FMCGs, and apparel, setting the stage for a robust festive season. Volume growth was strong even after adjusting for price increases and a low base effect.

articles.headline: Novo Nordisk, Eli Lilly to launch anti-obesity pills in India by 2027
articles.summary: Oral weight-loss drugs Wegovy (semaglutide) from Novo Nordisk and orforglipron from Eli Lilly are expected to enter the Indian market in the first half of 2027. These pills, with 12-15% average weight-loss efficacy, aim to widen the prescribing base for obesity treatment.

articles.headline: Personal loans surge 16.9% on gold and FD-backed loans
articles.summary: Personal loans, comprising one-third of total bank credit, grew 16.9% year-on-year by August-end, driven by significant increases in gold loans (83.2%) and loans against fixed deposits. Housing loans also saw 11.1% growth. Credit card outstanding growth, however, slowed to 3.6%.

articles.headline: Digital NBFCs’ personal loan books expand 28%
articles.summary: Digital-first NBFCs' personal loan portfolios grew 28% to `1.54 lakh crore by June-end, despite a slight dip in outstanding loan accounts. The average outstanding balance per account increased by nearly 30%. Growth was strong among younger borrowers and those with limited credit histories.

articles.headline: Stricter CAFÉ III norms for automakers notified from April 2027
articles.summary: The government notified Corporate Average Fuel Economy (CAFÉ) III guidelines, mandating automakers to progressively reduce average fuel consumption of passenger vehicle fleets over five years starting April 2027. The norms introduce a credit and debit mechanism for compliance and recognise more clean technologies.

articles.headline: AI cheat sheets mar job tests as malpractice surges
articles.summary: Cheating in hiring assessments and interviews is surging, with 45% of assessments flagged for malpractice in FY26, up from 32.4% in FY22. AI-assisted cheating grew 50% year-on-year, involving deepfakes and AI-generated responses, prompting employers to innovate detection strategies.

articles.headline: SC raps UP Police for FIR against ‘unknown’ rider
articles.summary: The Supreme Court criticized the Uttar Pradesh Police for registering an FIR against an "unknown" motorcycle rider despite the complainant apprehending him on the spot. Justices Sanjay Kumar and Sanjeev Sachdeva questioned the credibility of the investigation, calling for an explanation.

articles.headline: INDIA bloc to hold MPs’ march, rallies against ECI and 'vote theft'
articles.summary: Nineteen INDIA bloc parties announced joint protests, including district-level marches (Oct 2-8), an MPs' march to ECI (Oct 6), and five rallies from November 1, against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and alleged electoral irregularities.

articles.headline: BJP calls INDIA bloc protests 'Save Dynasty' march, questions unity
articles.summary: Union Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan dismissed the INDIA bloc's 'Save Democracy' campaign as a 'Save Dynasty' march. He accused the opposition of attacking constitutional institutions and lacking a common agenda, instead of introspecting on electoral setbacks.

articles.headline: Sonam Wangchuk seeks to study Mizoram Peace Accord
articles.summary: Environmentalist Sonam Wangchuk met former Mizoram CM Zoramthanga to study the Mizo Peace Accord, which brought lasting peace to Mizoram. The 1986 Memorandum of Settlement ended two decades of strife, making Mizoram one of India's most peaceful states.

articles.headline: J&K parties seek action against chief, law secretaries for statehood query
articles.summary: J&K parties, excluding BJP, urged Speaker Abdul Rahim Rather to act against the chief secretary and law secretary for questioning the statehood resolution moved by CM Omar Abdullah. BJP MLAs termed the resolution "unconstitutional and illegal."

articles.headline: PM Modi and US President Trump review bilateral ties
articles.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi and US President Donald Trump held a telephone conversation, reviewing bilateral cooperation in trade, defence, energy, and critical technologies. They reaffirmed commitment to advancing the India-US Comprehensive Global Strategic Partnership.

articles.headline: BJP's Rajya Sabha picks in UP to balance equations
articles.summary: The BJP faces a challenge in selecting eight Rajya Sabha candidates from Uttar Pradesh to balance electoral, caste, and regional equations ahead of the 2027 Assembly polls. The party is considering a mix of fresh faces and those who lost the 2024 Lok Sabha election.

articles.headline: Sena (UBT) leader shot dead, party blames Shinde Camp
articles.summary: Pradeep Purnekar, a Sena (UBT) divisional head, was shot dead in Thane by masked assailants. His family accused former Thane mayor Meenakshi Shinde and her husband from the Shinde faction of orchestrating the killing, leading to demands for their arrest.

articles.headline: AICC faces renewed push to oust Punjab PCC president Warring
articles.summary: The Congress high command is under renewed pressure from senior Punjab leaders to replace PCC president Amrinder Singh Raja Warring, who faces rebellion. AICC may discuss picking a ‘neutral leader’ like Vijay Inder Singla or former CM CS Channi, ahead of Sachin Pilot's state visit.

articles.headline: Bengaluru to map properties outside tax net for expansion
articles.summary: Karnataka’s Greater Bengaluru development minister Krishna Byre Gowda announced plans to map properties outside the city’s tax network, assign unique IDs, and bring them into the tax system. This aims to expand the tax base and address resource imbalance among Bengaluru's city corporations.

articles.headline: Darjeeling ‘Toy Train’ enters Lonely Planet’s Top 50 Global Destinations
articles.summary: The Darjeeling Himalayan Railway (DHR), a UNESCO World Heritage Site, has been named among Lonely Planet’s 'Best in Travel 2027 list' as the “Best for a Toy Train journey.” It is the only Indian entry, apart from one in Gujarat, to receive this international recognition.

articles.headline: Naveen Jindal weighs `5 billion bid for EU steelmaker Celsa
articles.summary: Jindal Steel chairman Naveen Jindal is evaluating a `5 billion bid for European steelmaker Celsa, marking an attempt to expand his global steel business. The acquisition of Celsa, with 7.5 million tonnes capacity, could push Jindal's total steel capacity beyond 25 million tonnes.

articles.headline: Mumbai property registrations record strongest September ever
articles.summary: Mumbai recorded its strongest September ever for property registrations, with 12,560 units, up 4% year-on-year. Stamp duty collections rose 32% to `640 crore. Ongoing infrastructure upgrades and connectivity improvements supported housing demand across established and emerging corridors.

articles.headline: HDFC Capital and Shalimar Corp create `750 crore UP real estate platform
articles.summary: HDFC Capital Advisors and Shalimar Corp formed a `750 crore platform to develop residential and mixed-use projects across Lucknow, Varanasi, and Kanpur. The platform aims to create over 5 million sq ft of development potential and about 3,000 homes in Uttar Pradesh.

articles.headline: Vadilal Inds signs new supply deal with estranged group firm
articles.summary: Vadilal Industries signed a revised one-year supply agreement with estranged group entity Vadilal Enterprises (VEL) for marketing and distribution, effective November 1, 2026. This follows the expiration of their 10-year agreement and an internal promoter dispute.

articles.headline: Gold hallmarking charges rise, fraud concerns grow
articles.summary: Rising gold hallmarking charges are fueling concerns about fake stamps, particularly in tier-2, 3, and 4 cities, where consumer awareness is low. The All-India Gem and Jewellery Domestic Council reported that only 10% of 800 districts adequately understand BIS app verification.

articles.headline: Manufacturing sector GVA grows 9.6% in 2024-25
articles.summary: India's formal manufacturing sector saw broad-based growth in 2024-25, with Gross Value Added (GVA) increasing 9.6% to `26.9 lakh crore. The sector added 1.4 million workers, bringing the total workforce to 21 million, and industrial output rose 7.8% to `165.2 lakh crore.

articles.headline: CEA warns of challenging H2 as global rates rise
articles.summary: Chief Economic Adviser V Anantha Nageswaran stated that the second half of the current fiscal year will be challenging due to increased downside risks to global growth and rising interest rates worldwide. He affirmed Q1 GDP growth data as "credible and reliable."

articles.headline: Crisil pegs FY27 India growth at 7%
articles.summary: Ratings agency Crisil upgraded its FY27 GDP growth estimate for India to 7% from 6.6%, anticipating strong growth in the April-September period. Chief economist DK Joshi expects H1 to witness fast growth, with a slowdown in H2, projecting crude oil at $87-93 per barrel.

articles.headline: India may ease pulses import duties due to poor rains
articles.summary: The government is considering reducing import duties on chana (10%) and yellow peas (30%) to improve domestic availability and curb rising prices. Deficient monsoon rainfall and uneven distribution raise concerns over crop yields, particularly in Maharashtra and Karnataka.

articles.headline: Export schemes extended amid West Asia crisis
articles.summary: The government extended the RoDTEP and RoSCTL duty refund schemes for exporters by three months to December 31, 2026. Additionally, enhanced insurance cover against payment defaults for consignments to West Asia was continued until March 31, 2027, providing policy stability.

articles.headline: Industrial states delay Labour Codes adoption, employers in flux
articles.summary: Only 10 states/UTs have notified rules for at least some of the four Labour Codes, leaving employers in a flux due to divergent provisions. Major industrial states like Karnataka, Maharashtra, and Punjab are delaying finalization, creating compliance inconsistencies and potential disputes for pan-India businesses.

articles.headline: October market cheer may be missing after September rout
articles.summary: Investors face a challenging October despite historical market favourability, due to elevated crude oil prices, rising global bond yields, continued foreign selling, and a weak rupee. The Nifty fell 6% in September, with 23,000-23,100 seen as key resistance.

articles.headline: Over 50 companies rush to file DRHP filings in September
articles.summary: More than 50 companies filed Draft Red Herring Prospectuses (DRHPs) with Sebi in September, making it the busiest month in a year. This rush is driven by a regulatory deadline requiring audited annual results to be no more than six months old for filings.

articles.headline: Rupee recovers to 95.83 against dollar as crude prices ease
articles.summary: The Indian rupee closed stronger at 95.83 a dollar on Wednesday, recovering 15 paise from Tuesday's close. The currency's gain was attributed to easing crude oil prices, despite higher dollar demand in morning trade which had initially pushed it lower.

articles.headline: Hospital stocks slip after SC questions steep cancer drug markups
articles.summary: India’s hospital stocks fell after the Supreme Court questioned steep markups on cancer drugs and asked the government to probe allegations that hospitals force patients to buy from designated pharmacies. The court also considered a uniform 16% margin on all medicines.

articles.headline: Rating upgrades dip amid headwinds, but credit profile resilient
articles.summary: Rating upgrades decreased in H1 FY27 compared to the previous year, as companies face headwinds like the West Asia conflict, rising crude prices, and US tariff measures. Despite moderation, India Inc.'s credit profile remains resilient due to stronger balance sheets and liquidity.

articles.headline: Sebi orders direct refund to Growpital investors for unregistered CIS
articles.summary: Sebi will directly refund money to 5,208 investors who lost `192.88 crore through the unregistered collective investment scheme Growpital. The regulator appointed a nodal officer to oversee refunds, with 12% annual interest, from Growpital's escrow account.

articles.headline: Wall Street gains despite rise in bond yields, easing inflation data
articles.summary: US stocks gained on Wednesday, with the S&P 500 up 0.4%, after August inflation data showed a 3.4% rise, lower than the expected 3.7%. Despite the positive inflation surprise, Wall Street still faces pressure from rising 10-year Treasury yields, which hit 5.30%.

articles.headline: Oil prices rise on US-Iran talks stall, tight fuel markets
articles.summary: Oil prices rose on Wednesday, with Brent November futures up 0.6% to $103.19 a barrel, driven by stalled US-Iran talks and tight fuel markets. Brent is set for a 14% monthly gain, its biggest since July, while WTI eyes a 5.5% rise.

articles.headline: India’s external debt eases to 20.8% of GDP in June Q1
articles.summary: India’s external debt-to-GDP ratio moderated to 20.8% from 20.9% in Q1 FY27, despite a $15.4 billion rise in debt to $778.2 billion. Loans remain the largest component at 34.3%. US dollar-denominated debt contributed 54.8%.

articles.headline: Banks pay less for deposits, charge more for fresh loans in August
articles.summary: Banks paid less for fresh term deposits (down 18 bps to 5.67%) while charging more for new loans (up 9 bps to 8.61%) in August, widening the rate gap by 27 basis points. This divergence, driven by private banks, has been observed since March.

articles.headline: RBI’s net short forward position rises to $200 billion in August
articles.summary: The Reserve Bank of India’s net short forward position increased to $200 billion in August, up from $136 billion in July, despite some long positions being added. This reflects sell-buy swaps and the RBI's inability to allow complete maturity of shorts amid rupee depreciation pressures.

articles.headline: New ExIm trade rules pose challenges for card-based service imports
articles.summary: New international trade payment regulations require detailed reporting of service imports on RBI's digital platforms, including card-based payments. This raises ambiguity for individuals and businesses on how to report personal card purchases for overseas services, as banks currently lack clear mechanisms for such data collection.

articles.headline: Telcos, consumer groups clash over TRAI’s 5G slicing norms
articles.summary: Telecom operators and consumer groups clashed over TRAI's proposals for 5G network slicing, coverage map accuracy, and financial disincentives for missing quality benchmarks. Telcos argue 5G slicing is an internal parameter, while consumer groups advocate strict utilization benchmarks.

articles.headline: Haier, Godrej, Blue Star faulted for fake e-waste claims
articles.summary: Tax authorities faulted appliance makers Haier, Godrej & Boyce, and Blue Star for failing to detect fabricated documents by a spurious recycler, who did no e-waste work, while they claimed `714,000 in tax credits. Indian officials accused them of relying on fake claims to meet green goals.

articles.headline: Nirav Modi loses bid to prevent sale of London apartment
articles.summary: A UK court approved the sale of a luxury London apartment linked to Nirav Modi, the jeweller accused of `2 billion PNB fraud. The `3.75 million pound sale proceeds will be placed in a secure account after trust liabilities are cleared, supporting the Enforcement Directorate's claim.

articles.headline: Electric 2-wheeler sales cross 1.5 million in 9 months
articles.summary: Electric two-wheeler sales in India surpassed 1.5 million units in the first nine months of 2026, exceeding total 2025 sales. Registrations rose 7.7% month-on-month in September to 1.97 lakh units, driven by rising fuel prices and lower running costs. Top automakers lead the market.

articles.headline: Palmonas leverages offline stores and unique designs for revenue surge
articles.summary: Demi-fine jewellery brand Palmonas, led by cofounder Pallavi Mohadikar, achieved a 5x revenue surge by leveraging its 105 offline stores and loyal repeat customers. The Pune-based startup focuses on unique designs and physical retail to compete in the growing market.

articles.headline: Apple plans smart-home hub launch, HomePod mini update in October
articles.summary: Apple is set to launch its long-delayed smart-home hub, code-named J490, and release the first update to the HomePod mini in October. This push aligns with hardware chief John Ternus's tenure, emphasizing devices and integrating AI into existing products.

articles.headline: Tech Mahindra board to consider bonus share proposal in October
articles.summary: Tech Mahindra’s board will consider a proposal to issue bonus shares during its October meeting, when it declares financial results for Q2 FY27. The company has not yet disclosed the bonus issue ratio, pending board approval.

articles.headline: GCCs build in-house forward deployed engineering chops
articles.summary: Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE) job postings in India surged 800% year-on-year (April 2025-26) as Global Capability Centres (GCCs) increasingly build in-house FDE capabilities to deploy AI for parent companies. This shift could bring $200-300 million worth of FDE consulting work in-house.

articles.headline: Muted Q2 awaits IT firms amid AI deflation, pricing pressures
articles.summary: India's large IT services companies are expected to report another quarter of weak results in Q2 FY27, impacted by AI-led revenue deflation and soft demand. TCS and Infosys project muted growth, while HCLTech and Tech Mahindra are anticipated to outperform.

articles.headline: India sweeps all compound team archery golds, secures Olympic quota
articles.summary: India's archers swept all three compound team gold medals (men's, women's, mixed) at the Asian Games. Chikitha Taniparthi and Sahil Jadhav secured an Olympic quota place in the compound mixed team event, which debuts at the 2028 Los Angeles Games.

articles.headline: FTC orders probe into Anthropic, OpenAI over AI safety concerns
articles.summary: The Federal Trade Commission (FTC) launched an industry-wide probe into Anthropic, OpenAI, and other AI labs. This first official enforcement action targets potential dangers from rogue AI agents, following incidents where AI hacked open-source platforms, raising fears of uncontrolled AI harming humans.

articles.headline: Israel to ramp up pilot checks after Flydubai flight scare
articles.summary: Israel will increase security checks on inbound pilots after a Flydubai co-pilot allegedly stabbed the pilot and attempted to crash a Dubai-Tel Aviv flight. PM Netanyahu instructed authorities to "ramp up security" on flights to Israel by both Israeli and non-Israeli carriers.

articles.headline: US upgrades Q2 GDP growth estimate to 2.2%
articles.summary: The US Commerce Department revised upwards its estimate for second-quarter GDP growth by 0.7 percentage points to 2.2%. The revision was driven by robust consumer spending, investment, and exports, with real estate and information sectors being major contributors.

articles.headline: Citadel CEO Ken Griffin donates $3 billion to Carnegie Mellon University
articles.summary: Citadel CEO Ken Griffin donated $3 billion to Carnegie Mellon University, the largest single gift to a US university. $2 billion will fund a new 35-acre campus in Miami focused on societal challenges; the rest goes to Pittsburgh's computer science program and other projects.

articles.headline: Russia warns NATO of nuclear attack over Kaliningrad isolation
articles.summary: Russia warned NATO it would use nuclear weapons to defend its territory if the alliance attempted to isolate Kaliningrad, a Russian exclave bordering the Baltic Sea. Moscow accused NATO of a "dangerous and reckless course" risking direct armed conflict.

articles.headline: China factory activity hits 5-month high in September
articles.summary: China's manufacturing sector expanded at its fastest pace in five months in September, with the PMI rising to 52.1 from 51.5 in August. Output grew at the fastest rate since April, and new export orders rose at the quickest pace in seven months, driven by stronger Asian market conditions.

articles.headline: US to double EB-5 Green Card fees from November 30
articles.summary: The US Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) will double fees for applying to the EB-5 investor program, effective November 30. This program grants permanent residency (Green Card) to foreign investors who invest capital into a US enterprise and create 10 full-time jobs.

articles.headline: MI5 warns of Beijing link to tech research espionage in UK
articles.summary: Britain's MI5 spy agency issued an alert warning that a Chinese organization, CGTRI, with "very strong ties" to Beijing's Ministry of State Security (MSS), funded academic research into AI, cybersecurity, and covert communications in the UK, posing a national security threat.

articles.headline: FTC Probes OpenAI, Anthropic on AI Product Safety Concerns
articles.summary: The Federal Trade Commission is investigating OpenAI, Anthropic, and other major AI firms concerning the safety of their products. This probe follows recent high-profile cybersecurity incidents and aims to ensure compliance with consumer protection laws and address growing concerns about AI risks.

articles.headline: British PM Considers EU Re-entry Options Amid Brexit Harm
articles.summary: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham stated the UK should explore options for its future relationship with the European Union, including potential rejoining the bloc, single market, or customs union. He argued Brexit has "done more harm than good" and plans to gauge public opinion on these possibilities.

articles.headline: Archer's Father Sells Harvester for Asian Games Gold
articles.summary: Chikitha Taniparthi won two compound archery gold medals at the Asian Games, securing an LA 2028 Olympics berth. Her father, a small farmer, sold his harvester and took loans to fund her training, expressing surprise at her double victory and lamenting a lack of government incentives.

articles.headline: BJP Criticizes Karnataka's Urdu Festival Plan at Vidhana Soudha
articles.summary: The BJP criticized Karnataka's proposal to host an Urdu festival at Vidhana Soudha, labeling it 'vote-bank politics' and an appeasement bid. Former minister Suresh Kumar questioned the event's priority and its symbolism concerning Kannada identity.

articles.headline: Massive Drug Haul: ₹3,000 Crore Heroin and Meth Seized, 5 Pakistanis Held
articles.summary: Gujarat ATS and the Coast Guard arrested five Pakistani nationals on an Iranian dhow, seizing 526kg of heroin and meth valued at Rs 3,000 crore. The contraband, destined for Pakistan via Haji Salim, was intercepted west of Lakshadweep after a 16-day pursuit, dismantling a Pakistan-linked narcotics network.

articles.headline: Karnataka CM to Address Rs 38,000 Crore Contractor Pending Bills
articles.summary: Karnataka CM DK Shivakumar agreed to discuss pending contractor bills totaling Rs 38,000 crore, blaming the previous BJP government for sanctioning works without budgetary provisions. He challenged contractors to provide evidence of commission demands.

articles.headline: MRPL Refinery Blast Kills One, Injures Twelve in Karnataka
articles.summary: A blast and fire at a Mangalore Refinery and Petrochemicals Ltd (MRPL) unit killed one contract worker and injured 12. The explosion occurred due to a ruptured high-pressure separator in the Coker Hydrotreater Unit. An FIR names unit and MRPL officials.

articles.headline: Modi, Trump Discuss Ties Amid US Sanctions Threat on Russian Energy
articles.summary: PM Modi and US President Trump reviewed bilateral cooperation, with Modi raising concerns over US sanctions impacting countries buying Russian oil. External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar also discussed the issue with US Secretary of State Marco Rubio.

articles.headline: Small Savings Interest Rates Unchanged for Tenth Quarter
articles.summary: Interest rates on small savings schemes, including PPF (7.1%) and NSC (7.7%), remain unchanged for the tenth consecutive quarter from October to December. The Sukanya Samriddhi Scheme continues to offer 8.2% interest.

articles.headline: SC Slams UP Police for 'Cover-up' in Accident FIR
articles.summary: The Supreme Court criticized Uttar Pradesh police for a "cover-up job" in a road accident FIR, questioning the registration against an unknown person when the accused was apprehended on-site, prompting the court to summon the officer.

articles.headline: Nilekani Taskforce Proposes Exam 'Debundling' and Local Test Centers
articles.summary: The Nandan Nilekani-led task force suggests 'debundling' exam responsibilities among agencies and establishing test centers in every district with a common calendar to improve access and standards for major exams.

articles.headline: Student Stabbed to Death Near Bengaluru College
articles.summary: A 19-year-old BCom student was fatally stabbed near his Bengaluru college following an argument with a group of youths. Police are investigating a possible connection to a girl known to those involved.

articles.headline: Tata Trusts File Caveats Amid Internal Governance Dispute
articles.summary: Six Tata Trusts filed caveats with the Maharashtra charity commissioner to prevent adverse orders without a hearing. This follows a complaint by Venu Srinivasan alleging Sir Dorabji Tata Trust meddled in Tata Sons' affairs, amidst controversy over trust governance.

articles.headline: Court Frames Charges Against Jharkhand CM Hemant Soren in Land Scam
articles.summary: A PMLA court in Ranchi framed charges against Jharkhand CM Hemant Soren in a money-laundering case linked to alleged illegal land acquisition. Soren denies the allegations, and his trial is set to begin November 30.

articles.headline: Congress, BJP Leaders Spar Over Janata Jodo Jagruti Yatra
articles.summary: Karnataka Congress president BK Hariprasad and BJP chief BY Vijayendra engaged in a political spat as the Congress launched its yatra from Vijayendra's constituency, targeting BJP's strategies for the 2028 elections.

articles.headline: SC Signals Dismissal of Bengal's Plea Against Cong Candidate's Bail
articles.summary: The Supreme Court indicated it would dismiss West Bengal's appeal challenging interim bail for Congress candidate Milan Pradhan in the Nandigram bypoll case, citing a lengthy court board and declining an urgent hearing.

articles.headline: India's First Commercial Thermal Payload to Launch Via SpaceX
articles.summary: SatLeo Labs will launch TAPAS-1, India's first dedicated commercial thermal payload, via SpaceX Falcon 9 on October 1. The payload uses infrared sensing for climate, agriculture, and disaster monitoring, enabling temperature pattern analysis.

articles.headline: Farm Fires Decline Sharply in Punjab, Haryana Ahead of Winter
articles.summary: Punjab and Haryana have significantly reduced stubble-burning incidents, improving Delhi's winter pollution outlook. Punjab fires dropped from 83,000 (2020) to 5,100 (2025), but challenges for small farmers and crop diversification persist.

articles.headline: India's Monsoon Ends with 13% Deficit, Fourth Lowest Since 2001
articles.summary: India's summer monsoon concluded with a 13% rainfall deficit, its fourth lowest since 2001. While a normal winter monsoon is forecast for parts of the south, this overall deficit raises concerns for agricultural output.

articles.headline: Reliance Executive Dhanraj Nathwani Named SP's Rajya Sabha Candidate
articles.summary: Dhanraj Parimal Nathwani, Group President at Reliance Industries, is Samajwadi Party's surprise Rajya Sabha pick from Uttar Pradesh, filing nominations alongside Ram Gopal Yadav.

articles.headline: INDIA Bloc Plans Nationwide 'Save Democracy' Agitation
articles.summary: The INDIA bloc will launch a nationwide 'Save Democracy' agitation starting October 2, demanding ballot papers for future polls and the resignation of CEC Gyanesh Kumar, with a major rally planned in Delhi on November 1.

articles.headline: Bombay HC Stays Sachin Waze's Bail in Antilia Case
articles.summary: The Bombay High Court has stayed the interim bail granted to former police officer Sachin Waze in the Antilia bomb scare and Mansukh Hiran murder cases, suspending his release after nearly 2,000 days in custody.

articles.headline: Apple Pay Launches in India with Axis Bank Partnership
articles.summary: Apple Pay has officially launched in India, initially supporting Axis Bank Visa and Mastercard credit cardholders for contactless payments. The service aims to leverage India's growing NFC infrastructure.

articles.headline: Simple Energy Raises ₹1,750 Crore to Scale EV Production
articles.summary: Electric two-wheeler maker Simple Energy secured Rs 1,750 crore in a Series C funding round to expand manufacturing capacity to 30,000 units monthly, boost R&D, and grow its distribution network.

articles.headline: Shubman Gill's Record Double Century Seals India's Series Win
articles.summary: Shubman Gill scored the fastest ODI double century (223* off 133 balls) as India chased down 406 runs to defeat West Indies by eight wickets, clinching the three-match series.

articles.headline: Indian Archers Sweep Compound Golds, Secure Olympic Berth
articles.summary: Indian compound archers won all three available gold medals at the Asian Games (men's, women's, mixed teams), with the mixed team's victory securing a 2028 LA Olympics berth.

articles.headline: Neeru Dhanda Wins Second Asian Games Gold in Trap Mixed Team
articles.summary: Neeru Dhanda and Kynan Chenai secured gold in the trap mixed team event at the Asian Games, setting a new Asian record. Dhanda became the first Indian woman with two trap golds.

articles.headline: Lovlina Borgohain Reaches Second Consecutive Asian Games Boxing Final
articles.summary: Olympic bronze medallist Lovlina Borgohain became the first Indian woman boxer to reach back-to-back Asian Games finals, winning her 75kg semifinal. She will face China's Ziyi Bao for gold.

articles.headline: Sunil Kumar Wins Wrestling Bronze, Becomes First Two-Time Medallist
articles.summary: Sunil Kumar won bronze in the men's 87kg Greco-Roman wrestling at the Asian Games, becoming the first Indian to win two medals in this category at the Games.

articles.headline: India Women's Hockey Team Reaches Asian Games Final, Aims for Gold
articles.summary: The Indian women's hockey team defeated South Korea 2-0 in the Asian Games semifinal, securing a spot in the gold-medal match against defending champions China.

articles.headline: Brazil Captain Raphinha to Miss India Friendly Due to Injury
articles.summary: Brazil's captain Raphinha has been ruled out of the upcoming friendly against India in Kolkata due to a thigh injury sustained in a previous match. No replacement player will be called up.

articles.headline: India's Fiscal Deficit Reaches 41.9% of Target by August
articles.summary: India's fiscal deficit hit Rs 7.1 lakh crore by August, 41.9% of the budget estimate, driven by increased capital expenditure and higher subsidy outlays, while net tax revenue saw modest growth.

articles.headline: Vithya Ramraj Credits Family Struggles for Sports Career
articles.summary: Athlete Vithya Ramraj shared that her entry into sports was driven by her family's financial challenges, enabling access to food and facilities. She expressed gratitude for government support and emphasized athlete autonomy.

articles.headline: Southwest Monsoon Ends with 13% Deficit, Worst Since 2015
articles.summary: India's southwest monsoon concluded with a 13% deficit, the lowest rainfall since 2015, attributed to El Niño. Southern and Eastern regions faced the most significant rainfall shortfall, impacting kharif yields.

articles.headline: Coca-Cola Considers December IPO Filing for Indian Bottling Unit
articles.summary: Coca-Cola is reportedly considering a December draft prospectus filing for its Indian bottling unit, Hindustan Coca-Cola Beverages, aiming for a $1 billion IPO and a valuation of $10 billion.

articles.headline: Reliance Industries Raises ₹13,000 Crore via 10-Year Bonds
articles.summary: Reliance Industries Ltd (RIL) secured ₹13,000 crore through 10-year bonds at a 7.9% coupon, raising its September domestic bond borrowings to ₹25,000 crore to ensure funding certainty.

articles.headline: DoorDash Opens First India Office in Hyderabad, Plans 3,000+ Headcount
articles.summary: DoorDash launched its first India office in Hyderabad with 500 employees, planning to scale to over 3,000 within two years to support its global platform and customer experience.

articles.headline: Apr-Aug Fiscal Deficit Widens to ₹7.1 Trillion
articles.summary: India's fiscal deficit reached ₹7.1 trillion (42% of BE) in April-August, up 19% year-on-year, driven by higher capital expenditure and a 25% surge in major subsidies.

articles.headline: HDFC Bank Appoints V N Srivatsan as Chief Compliance Officer
articles.summary: HDFC Bank appointed V N Srivatsan, currently with ICICI Bank, as its Chief Compliance Officer (CCO) for a three-year term, effective January 4, 2027.

articles.headline: Traders Call Off 'No UPI Day' Protest After Meeting Finance Minister
articles.summary: Trade bodies ended their 'No UPI Day' protest after meeting Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman, who assured consideration of their concerns regarding proposed Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) changes.

articles.headline: Cabinet Approves ₹1.86 Trillion Green Energy Corridor Phase-III
articles.summary: The Union Cabinet approved the Green Energy Corridor Phase-III (GEC-III) scheme with a ₹1.86 trillion outlay to develop transmission infrastructure for 135 GW of renewable energy and deploy 50 GWh of battery storage by 2033.

articles.headline: Special Intensive Revision Exclusions Shrink Electorate
articles.summary: Opposition parties are challenging the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise, which excluded 130 million electors, reducing the electorate in many states to 2015 levels, raising concerns over electoral integrity.

articles.headline: Sebi Aims for Seamless Digital FPI Onboarding, Explores Bond Indices
articles.summary: Sebi and RBI are collaborating to create a fast, seamless, and digital onboarding process for foreign portfolio investors (FPIs), while Sebi also considers bond indices for exchange trading.

articles.headline: Inox Clean Energy Files DRHP for ₹10,000 Crore IPO
articles.summary: Inox Clean Energy, part of INOXGFL Group, filed its DRHP for a ₹10,000 crore IPO, comprising an ₹8,000 crore fresh issue and a ₹2,000 crore offer for sale, to repay borrowings.

articles.headline: KPI Green Energy to Acquire 507.9 Mw Wind Capacity for ₹2,410 Crore
articles.summary: KPI Green Energy has entered a binding offer to acquire 507.9 MW of operational wind capacity in Gujarat through its subsidiaries for ₹2,410 crore.

articles.headline: Multiple Companies Open Special Window for Physical Securities Transfer
articles.summary: IRIS RegTech Solutions, Zee Media, SPL Industries, and Kkalpana Industries have opened one-year windows for shareholders to re-lodge physical securities transfer requests, with transferred shares subject to a one-year lock-in.

articles.headline: Chandra Family Link Surfaces in Karnataka Business Unit
articles.summary: A connection between the Chandra family and Venu has emerged concerning a Karnataka business unit, raising questions about potential dealings.

articles.headline: The Catch Behind Lower-Cost EVs Powered by BaaS Explained
articles.summary: Industry executives discuss the advantages of Battery-as-a-Service (BaaS) for lower-cost electric vehicles, with Tata Motors highlighted as a key player adopting this strategy.

articles.headline: Opsec Pricing Discussions Involve Significant Financial Figures
articles.summary: Discussions around Opsec pricing involve substantial financial figures, with amounts of $30 billion and 2,000 crore mentioned in relation to the pricing strategy.

articles.headline: Pilot Averts Flydubai Hijacking Attempt After Co-Pilot Attack
articles.summary: An Indian pilot landed a Flydubai flight safely in Saudi Arabia after his co-pilot allegedly attacked him en route to Tel Aviv. Passengers subdued the attacker, preventing a potential disaster.

articles.headline: LeT Commander Active in J&K Since 2022 Killed in Budgam
articles.summary: Mohammad Asif alias Hashim Moosa, a Pakistan-based Lashkar-e-Taiba commander active in Jammu and Kashmir since 2022, was killed in Budgam, marking a significant breakthrough for security forces.

articles.headline: Amit Shah Vows to End Punjab Drug Menace by December 2029
articles.summary: Union Home Minister Amit Shah pledged to eradicate the drug menace in Punjab by December 31, 2029, if the BJP forms the next government, criticizing the AAP government's handling of the issue.

articles.headline: Congress Candidate Milan Pradhan Released on Interim Bail for Nandigram
articles.summary: Milan Pradhan, Congress candidate for the Nandigram byelection, was granted interim bail and began campaigning after alleging police pressure to withdraw his candidacy during his 12-day custody.

articles.headline: Reliance Executive's Samajwadi Party Entry Spices Up Rajya Sabha Polls
articles.summary: The Samajwadi Party nominated Reliance Industries executive Dhanraj Parimal Nathwani, alongside Ram Gopal Yadav, for the Rajya Sabha elections, adding a corporate figure to the UP political landscape.

articles.headline: ₹3,000 Crore Drug Haul: 5 Pakistanis Held Off Lakshadweep Coast
articles.summary: The Indian Coast Guard and Gujarat ATS seized 526 kg of methamphetamine and heroin, valued over ₹3,000 crore, from an Iranian boat near Lakshadweep, detaining five Pakistani nationals.

articles.headline: Supreme Court Rules Out Blanket Firecracker Ban for Diwali
articles.summary: The Supreme Court permitted the use of "green" firecrackers, refusing a total ban due to public sentiments, while seeking a CPCB report on barium content to determine permissible types and timings.

articles.headline: Archers' Triple Gold Haul Boosts India's Asian Games Standing
articles.summary: Indian compound archers secured three gold medals at the Asian Games (mixed, women's, men's teams), significantly improving India's medal tally and securing a 2028 LA Olympics spot.

articles.headline: Punjab Congress Chief Warring Offers Resignation Amid Infighting
articles.summary: Punjab Congress president Amarinder Singh Raja Warring has offered to resign amidst ongoing factionalism within the state unit, with former minister Vijay Inder Singla reportedly being considered as a successor.

articles.headline: Woman, Friend Convicted in 'Blue Drum' Husband Murder Case
articles.summary: A Meerut court convicted Muskan Rastogi and her partner Sahil Shukla for the 2025 murder of her husband, merchant navy officer Saurabh Rajput, whose body was found dismembered in a blue drum.

articles.headline: Goyal Pitches for Deeper India-US Economic Ties Beyond Trade
articles.summary: Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal urged deeper India-US economic ties, focusing on investment, manufacturing, and supply chains, and invited US firms to expand in India.
